definitions.type: subset of Euclidean ℝ^{n+1}, identified with ℝ^n×ℝ
definitions.definition: F=E×I. Under the coordinate identification (x,t)↔(x_1,…,x_n,t), the distance between (x,t) and (y,u) is sqrt(‖x-y‖₂²+|t-u|²). For n=0, ℝ^0 consists of its unique empty coordinate vector.

definitions.type: operator on a metric space X, a positive real s, a positive real δ and a subset A⊆X, valued in [0,∞]
definitions.definition: For a metric space X, s>0, δ>0 and A⊆X, Hscale(s,δ,A)=inf{Σ_{i≥0}(diam U_i)^s : A⊆⋃_{i≥0}U_i and diam U_i≤δ for every i}. Covers are countable (finite covers are padded by empty sets). The diameter is the supremum of pairwise distances, with diameter of the empty set zero and unbounded diameter +∞; an empty member contributes zero. Sums, infima and suprema are in [0,∞], with inf ∅=∞. Covers are not required to be measurable.

definitions.type: operator on subsets of extended metric spaces, valued in [0,∞]
definitions.definition: For A⊆X, hdim(A)=sup{a∈[0,∞):Hnative(a,A)=∞}, with the empty supremum equal to zero and real exponents embedded into [0,∞]. This is the native dimH definition (the exponent is represented by a nonnegative real). It is the usual Hausdorff dimension; in particular the definition assigns zero to the empty set.
D=hdim(E). Once finiteness is proved, real arithmetic with D means its unique finite real representative; no finiteness is assumed by this definition.

definitions.type: operator on a real exponent a and a subset A of an extended metric space X with its Borel measurable structure, valued in [0,∞]
definitions.definition: Hnative(a,A) denotes the native value (MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a)(A) on X. Its full covering formula is sup_{r∈(0,∞]} inf_{T:ℕ→Set X, A⊆⋃_i T_i, ∀i ediam(T_i)≤r} Σ_i w_a(T_i), where w_a(T)=0 for T empty and w_a(T)=(ediam T)^a otherwise; all diameters and operations here are extended nonnegative real operations, including extended real powers. Thus empty sets are zero even at exponent zero. The native definition is the Borel measure Measure.mkMetric(r↦r^a). For ordinary metric spaces ediam is the extended-valued supremum of ordinary distances.

inputs.statement: E is bounded. For every δ>0 and every s>0, E has a finite cover by sets of diameter at most δ and finite s-cost, so Hscale(s,δ,E)<∞. Also 0≤D≤n, in particular hdim(E)=D is finite and can be identified with a real number. If n=0, then E=ℝ^0 is the singleton and D=0.
Let α be a measurable space, μ a measure on α, β a countable type and f:β→α→[0,∞]. If every f_i is μ-almost-everywhere measurable, then ∫⁻_α Σ_{i:β} f_i(a) dμ(a)=Σ_{i:β} ∫⁻_α f_i(a) dμ(a).
source_conditions: α has a measurable space structure and μ is a measure on it.
For every i∈β, f_i is μ-almost-everywhere measurable.

inputs.statement: For any real endpoints a,b, Lebesgue measure of the closed interval [a,b] is ENNReal.ofReal(b-a), namely max(b-a,0) embedded in [0,∞].
For any real endpoints a,b, Lebesgue measure of the open interval (a,b) is ENNReal.ofReal(b-a), namely max(b-a,0) embedded in [0,∞].

output.statement: For every real s>0 and every real δ>0, Hscale(s,δ,E)≤Hscale(s+1,δ,F).

locals.declaration: Fix ε>0, to be sent to zero.
Take any countable δ-cover V of F, allowing empty padding members.

locals.type: sequence of finite nonnegative real numbers
locals.declaration: Define ρ_i=diam V_i; since V is a δ-cover, 0≤ρ_i≤δ.
Define A_i as the projection of V_i onto ℝ^n.
Define B_i as the last-coordinate projection of V_i.

locals.type: sequence of open subsets of ℝ, each empty or a bounded open interval
locals.declaration: If V_i is nonempty, set J_i=(inf B_i-η_i/2,sup B_i+η_i/2); otherwise set J_i=∅.
Define f_i(t)=ρ_i^s 1_{J_i}(t), with the nonnegative real coefficient embedded in [0,∞].

argument.text: Fix s>0, δ>0 and ε>0. Define c=Hscale(s,δ,E). N002 gives a finite δ-cover of E with finite s-cost, so c<∞. Thus c can be integrated as a finite nonnegative constant.

Take any countable δ-cover V of F and write ρ_i=diam V_i, A_i=π_{ℝ^n}(V_i), B_i=π_ℝ(V_i). Coordinate projections decrease distances by the Euclidean distance formula; therefore diam A_i≤ρ_i and diam B_i≤ρ_i≤δ. Set η_i=ε2^{-i-1}/(1+ρ_i^s)>0. For every nonempty V_i its projection B_i is nonempty and bounded: distances between all its points are at most δ, so its infimum and supremum are finite. Their difference is at most ρ_i. Define J_i=(inf B_i-η_i/2,sup B_i+η_i/2), which contains B_i and has length at most ρ_i+η_i. For empty V_i set J_i=∅; such members have ρ_i^s=0 and are harmless. This is the same as discarding empty members while retaining the original indices. Thus every J_i is open and B_i⊆J_i. Neither V_i nor its projections need be measurable.

produces.statement: For every i, diam A_i≤ρ_i≤δ, B_i⊆J_i, and J_i is either empty or an open interval of length at most ρ_i+η_i; η_i=ε2^{-i-1}/(1+ρ_i^s)>0.

argument.text: For any t∈I, the A_i with t∈J_i cover E: for any x∈E some V_i contains (x,t), and then x∈A_i and t∈B_i⊆J_i. By F002 this is a δ-cover, whose s-cost is at most Σ_iρ_i^s 1_{J_i}(t). Hence c≤Σ_iρ_i^s 1_{J_i}(t) for every t∈I. Define f_i(t)=ρ_i^s 1_{J_i}(t). Every f_i is nonnegative and Borel measurable because J_i is open and its coefficient is a fixed finite nonnegative real. In particular it is almost-everywhere measurable for Lebesgue measure restricted to I.

produces.statement: For every t∈I, c≤Σ_i f_i(t), where f_i(t)=ρ_i^s1_{J_i}(t); each f_i is Borel measurable and hence Lebesgue-almost-everywhere measurable for the restricted measure on I.

argument.text: Integrate F003 against Lebesgue measure restricted to I. Its total mass is one by M007 with endpoints 0,1. Monotonicity of the nonnegative integral, the integral of a constant, and M005 applied to the nonnegative measurable series yield c≤Σ_i∫_I f_i(t)dt=Σ_iρ_i^s|J_i∩I|. Here the integral of a constant times a measurable indicator is that constant times its set's measure, directly the simple-function integral formula. By M008 and monotonicity of measure, |J_i∩I|≤|J_i|≤ρ_i+η_i (the empty case is zero). Consequently c≤Σ_iρ_i^s|J_i∩I|≤Σ_iρ_i^{s+1}+Σ_iη_iρ_i^s≤Σ_iρ_i^{s+1}+ε, because η_iρ_i^s=ε2^{-i-1}ρ_i^s/(1+ρ_i^s)≤ε2^{-i-1} and Σ_{i≥0}2^{-i-1}=1. All series are nonnegative; their order comparisons and splitting are valid also when a sum is infinite.

produces.statement: c≤Σ_iρ_i^{s+1}+ε for the arbitrary δ-cover V and arbitrary ε>0.

argument.text: If Σ_iρ_i^{s+1}=∞, the desired bound c≤Σ_iρ_i^{s+1} is immediate. If the sum is finite, F004 for all ε>0 gives that bound by letting ε↓0. Since V was any δ-cover of F, taking the infimum of its (s+1)-costs gives Hscale(s,δ,E)=c≤Hscale(s+1,δ,F). The construction of J depended on ε, but c and this cover's cost did not, so the limit is legitimate. Discharge the arbitrary-cover restrictions and s>0,δ>0,ε>0 restrictions and universally quantify s,δ. This proves the slicing inequality.

applications.bindings: Set α=ℝ with its Borel measurable structure, μ=Lebesgue measure restricted to I, β=ℕ and use f_i from S003.

The series index is ℕ, a countable type.
F003 proves Borel measurability of every f_i, hence almost-everywhere measurability for μ.

applications.bindings: Set a=0 and b=1; the interval [a,b] is I.
For each nonempty V_i set a=inf B_i-η_i/2 and b=sup B_i+η_i/2, so (a,b)=J_i; empty members contribute zero separately.
